profile.summary: Chroma is a generative model that designs proteins: it samples all-atom structures of single chains and complexes, and the matching sequences, by reversing a diffusion process. The user can sample freely or steer the sampling with composable conditioners for symmetry, substructure, shape, fold class or a text caption. It can also redesign the sequence and side chains of a structure given to it.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract; README: introduction, Sampling, Design, Conditioners

summary_quotes.text: a generative model for proteins and protein complexes that can directly sample novel protein structures and sequences, and that can be conditioned to steer the generative process towards desired properties and functions
Chroma achieves protein design as Bayesian inference under external constraints, which can involve symmetries, substructure, shape, semantics and even natural-language prompts

As a joint model of structure and sequence, Chroma can also be used for common protein modeling tasks such as [generating sequences given backbones](#design), packing side-chains, and scoring designs.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Chroma uses a diffusion process designed to match the conformational statistics of polymer ensembles: structures are corrupted towards collapsed polymer noise and a network learns to denoise them. The denoiser is a random graph neural network with long-range connectivity, inspired by N-body algorithms, which scales sub-quadratically with the number of residues, plus a layer that solves for a global structure from predicted inter-residue geometries. A second graph-based design network generates sequence and side chains, and conditional random fields are used for the sequence. Conditioners are PyTorch modules that transform the state or add energy, and the total energy is backpropagated so that any composition of them can be sampled with annealed Langevin dynamics.

quotes.text: we introduce a diffusion process that respects the conformational statistics of polymer ensembles
We parameterize this in terms of a random graph neural network with long-range connectivity inspired by efficient

Internally, Chroma uses diffusion modeling, equivariant graph neural networks, and conditional random fields to efficiently sample all-atom structures with a complexity that is sub-quadratic in the number of residues.
each Conditioner is a function that modifies the state and/or energy of a protein system in a differentiable way

we add on the diffusion energy to the output of the Conditioner(s) and then backpropagate the total energy through all intermediate transformations to compute the unconstrained forces that are compatible with generic sampling SDE such as annealed Langevin Dynamics

sections.title: Design modes and conditioners
sections.body: The design network is diffusion-aware: it was trained to predict sequence and side chains not only for natural structures at diffusion time t=0 but for noisy structures at all times. The design_t parameter therefore trades exact design (t=0.0) against robust design in a neighbourhood of the target backbone (t=0.5, the repository default), which the developers report improves one-shot refolding. Predefined conditioners cover symmetry, substructure, shape, secondary structure, domain class (Pfam, CATH, taxonomy), text captions and subsequence constraints, and new ones can be written as small PyTorch modules.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper describes two versions of the model, v.0 and v.1, used for its large unconditional sample sets, and notes an overrepresentation of alpha helices in v.1 under low-temperature sampling. The code is on GitHub and on PyPI as generate-chroma; the weights are downloaded at run time from Generate Biomedicines with a registered access token, so a result should name the code commit or package version, the weights the run downloaded, and the sampling settings (design_t, langevin_factor, inverse_temperature, sde_func). This page read the code at commit 501f474a.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: For generation: the chain lengths wanted and optional conditioners (symmetry group, substructure, shape, class labels, text caption, subsequence). For design: a protein structure in PDB or mmCIF form, with an optional selection of residues to redesign.

strengths.text: One model covers both generation and design: unconditional and conditional sampling of monomers and complexes, plus sequence redesign and side-chain packing of a given structure.

quotes.text: We provide a unified entry point to both unconditional and conditional protein design with the `Chroma.sample()` method.
Chroma's design network can be accessed separately to design, redesign, and pack arbitrary protein systems.

strengths.text: Conditioners compose, so symmetry, substructure, shape, class and text constraints can be combined without retraining, and new ones are a few lines of PyTorch.

run_guide.summary: Install Chroma, register a weights access token, and sample one 200-residue unconditional monomer to an mmCIF file.
prerequisites: An access token from https://chroma-weights.generatebiomedicines.com/, obtained by agreeing to the Chroma Parameters License. Free use is limited to academic and non-profit users.
Python with pip. The repository's requirements include torch, transformers==4.24.0, scikit_learn==1.1.2 and nglview==3.0.8; no Python version is pinned in the sources read.
A GPU is expected for useful speed: the README says large complexes take a few minutes on a commodity GPU. No GPU memory figure is given.

steps.title: Sample one protein
steps.shell:

chroma = Chroma()
protein = chroma.sample(chain_lengths=[200])

protein.to("sample.cif")
PY
